g.title: wav, mp3, flac, ogg or mp4 from any source. Real corpora are full of silence, hiss, clipping, test tones and phone-line audio.

aerosieve-cli on crates.io, the Rust library, and PyO3 bindings for Python. Batch runs inspect files in parallel with rayon and write results in input order, so shards are byte-identical to a single-threaded run.

axum and tokio. Memory per session is bounded by the utterance in progress, and sessions and frame sizes are capped. It held 1,000 concurrent streams on a 4-core laptop with verdicts at 14.8 ms p95 and zero failures.
Decode, segment and score compiled to a 1.7 MB WebAssembly module. Audio never leaves the page, and moving a threshold re-applies the policy to stored measurements without decoding again.
Converts to 16 kHz mono and levels loudness, but remembers the source full scale. Without that, leveling hid clipping; the benchmark caught this bug.

A hysteresis state machine modelled on Silero speech timestamps: start above one threshold, continue above a lower one, end after 500 ms of quiet. Bridging short pauses raised kept Hindi speech from 16.4 to 25.6 minutes. Batch mode is this same streaming segmenter fed the whole file.

Four deterministic numbers with no ML model: WADA-SNR, RMS level, clip ratio and spectral flatness over 300 to 3400 Hz. Measurement and judgement are separate, so thresholds change without re-reading audio.
Tar shards with audio plus JSON per clip, a manifest.jsonl and stats.json, ready for a training data loader.
Every dropped clip names its first failing check: low_snr, clipping, tonal, too_quiet, too_loud or silence. SieveBench caught 24,385 of 24,409 injected defects and named the right one for all but 2.
